title: Stance Adverbs in the Colonial City

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *francamente*, *indudablemente*, *en realidad*, *en rigor*, *propiamente dicho* and *lamentablemente* from B2 Unit 1: these are stance adverbs. A stance adverb steps outside the action and comments on the whole sentence: how sure, how exact or how sad the writer is. In writing about the colonial past they do two jobs: they mark a correction (*en realidad*) and they say how certain you are (*indudablemente*).

sections.title: Stance adverbs on colonial Mexico City
rows: Actually: you correct what people assume. En realidad, la vida de la calle era más mezclada que las castas. (Actually, life in the street was more mixed than the castes.)
Undoubtedly: you are sure. Indudablemente, Sor Juana fue una de las figuras más importantes de su época. (Undoubtedly, Sor Juana was one of the most important figures of her time.)
Strictly speaking: the exact fact. En rigor, el virreinato empezó en 1535. (Strictly speaking, the viceroyalty began in 1535.)
Unfortunately: your feeling about a fact. Lamentablemente, muchos documentos de la época se perdieron. (Unfortunately, many documents from that time were lost.)
In the strict sense; it follows the noun. El virreinato propiamente dicho empezó en 1535. (The viceroyalty in the strict sense began in 1535.)

sections.title: Where they go, and the commas
sections.content: A stance adverb can open the sentence, sit in the middle or close it, and a comma marks each edge: *En realidad, la calle era más mezclada.* / *La calle, en realidad, era más mezclada.* Right after the verb with no commas, the same word usually describes how something was done: *Sor Juana defendió rotundamente el derecho de las mujeres a estudiar*. *Apenas* and *precisamente* take no commas, because they point at the word right after them.

items.spanish: En realidad, las castas no describían bien la vida de la calle.
items.english: Actually, the castes did not describe life in the street well.

items.spanish: Sor Juana, indudablemente, quería tener tiempo para estudiar.
items.english: Sor Juana undoubtedly wanted to have time to study.

items.spanish: En rigor, la capital del virreinato era la Ciudad de México.
items.english: Strictly speaking, the capital of the viceroyalty was Mexico City.

items.spanish: Lamentablemente, no se conservan todos los retablos de aquella época.
items.english: Unfortunately, not all the altarpieces of that time have survived.

items.spanish: Precisamente en el convento tuvo Sor Juana tiempo para estudiar.
items.english: It was precisely in the convent that Sor Juana had time to study.

sections.content: Try the comma test: if you can put commas round the adverb and pause, it comments on the whole sentence. Use one stance adverb per sentence; two in a row sound heavy.
